<fantasai> Like :active in IE5!

<JoshT> ... can be a link, a form or submit button
<TabAtkins> q+
<JoshT> ... things that trigger a navigation
<astearns> q+

<kbabbitt> q+
<JoshT> ... could be confusing otherwise with forms
<JoshT> ... could say we have a navigation trigger element that also includes forms
<JoshT> ... current case is a pseudo class called trigger-link
<JoshT> ... activated on link you click

<kbabbitt> q-

<fantasai> +1

<bramus> q+

resolutions.resolution: make it a parse error to set string values or typed CSSOM values that require an element to resolve
resolutions.background: How/when do the `<length-percentage>` values that can be passed to the [rangeStart](https://drafts.csswg.org/web-animations-2/#dom-animation-rangestart)/[rangeEnd](https://drafts.csswg.org/web-animations-2/#dom-animation-rangeend) attributes on the Animation interface (or via [KeyframeAnimationOption](https://drafts.csswg.org/web-animations-2/#dom-keyframeanimationoptions-rangestart)) when assigni
irc: <JoshT> weinig: issue is that in the animations API in the JS API, there are places where you can set values
<JoshT> ...the setters have been defined to take strings
<JoshT> ... but the spec says 'parse this as...' and then a CSS property
<JoshT> ... in this case, the issue with range-start is that it takes what it should parse, and animation-range-end allows a length-percentage with any number
<JoshT> ... you can have length relative units
<JoshT> ... there's no spec on how to resolve those units
<JoshT> ... it's not happening during the style resolution
<JoshT> ... in other places, there's an API that takes a string and parses it as a CSS construct
<JoshT> ... normally we limit it to absolute units because we don't have a way to resolve relative units
<JoshT> ... in this bug it's about range-end, but we can take the same idea to other cases and limit to absolute length units and %. % are ok because they resolve later
<TabAtkins> I'm fine with this
<fantasai> sgtm
<JoshT> astearns: is it possible to define some way to resolve %?
<JoshT> weinig: % are not an issue. it's just relative units
<JoshT> astearns: so can we just pick something to resolve against like the root?
<JoshT> weinig: there are other options we could takw
<TabAtkins> q+
<JoshT> ... one is to treat it like media queries
<JoshT> ... say that relative units resolve against the initial style. could be different to the root
<JoshT> ... could say the units resolve against the target element of anim if it exists
<JoshT> ... then need to define what happens if target is null
<JoshT> ... and we need to pay the sync style resolution cost
<JoshT> ... or alt, we could define alternative time that these values get resolved against an element
<JoshT> ... i think they're all complicated
<JoshT> ... someone would need to figure out the tradeoffs
<JoshT> ... right now not implementable
<JoshT> ... want something implementable in a uniform way
<ydaniv> SGTM, until we define this properly
<JoshT> ... or maybe in future we'll have a generic way in JS to say 'given this element and unit, give me the computed px values'
<JoshT> ... someone in bug says this makes it useless
<JoshT> ... don't know if they were thinking if % weren't allowed
<JoshT> ydaniv: [that was me]. it is limiting, but it's OK to patch this now and spec it later

<JoshT> astearns: I agree and I'm fine, but if there is something that would be better for authors where we can arbitrarily pick an element without author choice, it might be better to do that than only have absolute units
<JoshT> ... if we do only absolute units now, we'll need an opt in to get the better behaviour
<JoshT> weinig: we can just do a parse error for relative units for now, and then not have a parse error in the future
<astearns> ack TabAtkins
<JoshT> TabAtkins: I agree with sam. don't want to resolve on root element
<JoshT> ... would rather make it parse-time invalid now
<fantasai> +1 to TabAtkins and weinig
<JoshT> weinig: my proposal is for both the string form and type CSS form
<TabAtkins> yeah there shoudln't be any difference between those two
<JoshT> ... you can do a typed value that is an em value, so we have to treat them the same here
<JoshT> PROPOSED: make it a parse error to set string values or typed CSSOM values that don't use absolute length units or percentages
<JoshT> weinig: one other clarificatio.n also precludes things like var, sibling-index() and anything that requires an element to resolve
<fantasai> sgtm
<fantasai> We can always relax restrictions once we figure out what's the best thing to do
<JoshT> ... but the implication is we're excluding anything that requires an element context
<JoshT> PROPOSED: make it a parse error to set string values or typed CSSOM values that require an element to resolve
<JoshT> RESOLVED: make it a parse error to set string values or typed CSSOM values that require an element to resolve
<JoshT> weinig: I've filed a bunch of issues like this. should I turn them all into a single issue that we can resolve on later?
<JoshT> ... or should we go through them one by one?
<JoshT> astearns: I'm fine with that if they're all basically the same decision
<JoshT> ... we can even make it an async proposal

resolutions.resolution: non existing pseudo-elements are considered to inherit from their ultimate originating element if you query the computed style
resolutions.background: https://github.com/web-platform-tests/wpt/pull/58814 introduces a test that passes in chrome by minting the inheritance tree, see https://github.com/web-platform-tests/wpt/pull/58814#issuecomment-4263707301
irc: <JoshT> TabAtkins: emilio pointed out that we have a WPT that expects a non-existant vt element to inherit from its non-existent parent
<JoshT> ... because vt pseudos aren't creating but you're asking for the computed style
<JoshT> ... emilio suggests that we inherit from the existing element rather than assuming a non-existent tree
<JoshT> ... the dev who did this had a crash and so he fixed it in a way and doesn't have opinions on which way it should go
<JoshT> ... I also agree
<JoshT> ... we probably should not be making assumptions about the state of a tree that doesn't exist
<JoshT> ... I suggest we take emilio 's suggestion
<JoshT> ... just say it's inheriting from the originating element
<bramus> sgtm
<JoshT> fantasai: so this is only while they don't exist? and then when we have a tree, do usual behaviour?
<JoshT> TabAtkins: yes?
<JoshT> s/yes?/yes/
<TabAtkins> el.gCS("::foo")
<JoshT> TabAtkins: and there is always in the query an originating element to look at
<JoshT> fantasai: there was a term for ultimate originating element
<JoshT> TabAtkins: yes
<JoshT> PROPOSED: non existing pseudo-elements are considered to inherit from their ultimate originating element if you query the computed style
<JoshT> astearns: any suggestions or objections?
<JoshT> RESOLVED: non existing pseudo-elements are considered to inherit from their ultimate originating element if you query the computed style
<JoshT> astearns: do we have any other situations like this?
<JoshT> TabAtkins: you can't ask for an element that might not exist. it's only pseudos where this can happen
<noamr> "A non-existent pseudo element falls in the forest. what style does it have?"
